fields.chosen: T1 ships `init` (creates `~/.auto/mail/` and the store), `docs` (the full command reference — an agent must be able to discover the surface it is being asked to use) and `reset` (G10 makes wiping a *supported operation*, and the harness needs it for isolation). `quickstart` and `doctor` are T4's, as the epic assigns them.
fields.title: T1 ships init, docs and reset; quickstart and doctor land in T4
fields.why: The project's CLI conventions call for `init` / `doctor` / `quickstart` / `docs` on every tool. The epic assigns "quickstart, doctor and agent-facing guidance" to **T4** and argues explicitly that adoption is a task, not a chore.

fields.chosen: The `mail-flow` scenario is a **single container** with one seeded host id and one `~/.auto`, containing **two registered project workspaces** (`/workspace/project-a`, `/workspace/project-b`). Each "agent" is a separate `auto` process invocation run in one of those workspaces.
fields.title: Two agents on one host = two workspaces in one container, not two containers
fields.why: T1's scenario must bring up "two agents on one host". `event-flow`'s pattern is one container per agent, each seeded with a **distinct `HOST_ID`** — that is precisely what makes it a *multi-host* scenario.

fields.chosen: In T1, "notify inline" means: `send` sets the receiver's pending flag inside its commit path, and the receiver's very next tool-call hook picks it up. No bus event is published by `auto mail send` in T1.
fields.title: Inline notification in T1 is the pending flag; the bus event waits for the daemon
fields.why: D-12 keeps inline notification as the fast path. The epic's container diagram draws the notification arriving over the bus (`DAEMON → BUS ⇢ HOOK`), but D-11 removes the daemon from T1 entirely.

fields.chosen: Binding identity is the **opaque `(manager, target)` pair G12 mandates**, derived by both sides from the *same* shared helper (`auto-shared/hooks.CaptureContext`), on a documented fallback ladder: `tmux` + `tmux_pane_id` → `ntm` + the NTM pane identifier → `cwd` + the resolved worktree path. **`subscribe` is the only writer of a binding row in T1** …
fields.title: A binding is keyed by the physical context hooks already capture
fields.why: The nudge needs to answer "does the agent that just fired this hook have mail?". The hook payload carries `session_id` and `cwd`; the `auto mail subscribe` process does **not** see `session_id` (it is a tool call, not the hook process).

fields.chosen: T1 defines `mail.Client` and ships the direct-store implementation only. It also ships a **conformance suite written against the interface** (the `auto-shared/rpc/conformance` pattern), run against that one implementation now.
fields.title: T1 defines the Client seam and ships one implementation, with the conformance suite written against the interface
fields.why: Seam 1 warns that "an abstraction with one implementation is a guess". D-11 settles that the MVP CLI binds the **direct-store** implementation and the RPC one is what the daemon uses.

fields.chosen: `auto mail ack <id>` always prints `{"id":…, "acked":true, "wonTransition":<bool>}` on stdout and exits **0** when the delivery exists. A loser gets `wonTransition:false` plus a one-line note on stderr naming who won it.
fields.title: Losing an ack race is a reported outcome, not an error exit
fields.why: G13 requires that a losing ack be "told, never silently treated as success". That fixes the payload, not the exit code, and the project convention reserves fail-fast exits for invalid CLI usage.

fields.chosen: The mail package maintains a **pending flag** — an empty marker file per bound subscription under `~/.auto/mail/alpha-flags/`. `send` creates the flag for each bound subscription inside the same commit path; `ack` removes it when that subscription's unacked count reaches zero.
fields.title: The no-mail hook path is gated by a pending-flag file, not a store read
fields.why: G8: "the common case — no pending mail — must cost about what a `stat` costs, and must never be able to stall or break the hook." Opening a SQLite file and running an indexed count is milliseconds, not a `stat`, and it happens on **every tool call of every agent on the host**.
